content.user_title: Evaluate Technology Choices with Structured Evidence
content.value_statement: Technology choices often lack consistent evidence and explicit trade-offs. This skill compares candidates across weighted dimensions and produces recommendations, risks, POC checks, and ADR-ready decisions.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies business goals, scale, team skills, and nonfunctional constraints before comparing options.
Compares candidates across functionality, performance, scalability, reliability, operations, community, learning, ecosystem, cost, and security.
Applies weights and scores to make evaluation priorities explicit.
Documents trade-offs, recommendation reasons, risks, mitigations, and follow-up actions.
Defines POC validation points for performance, resilience, and operational behavior.
Produces structured Markdown reports and ADR-ready decision records.
limitations: The skill relies on supplied requirements and facts; it does not retrieve current benchmarks or vendor data.
Default dimensions and weights are generic and require adjustment for each organization.
Example performance figures are illustrative and should not replace measurements in the target environment.
The skill plans POCs and migrations but does not execute deployments, benchmarks, or production changes.

use_cases.title: Select an Application Platform
use_cases.description: Compare frameworks or databases against product constraints, team experience, operating cost, and growth expectations.

use_cases.title: Plan an Infrastructure POC
use_cases.description: Define measurable tests for messaging, storage, or platform candidates before committing engineering resources.

use_cases.title: Document a Technical Decision
use_cases.description: Turn evaluation results into a reviewable recommendation with risks, mitigations, actions, and ADR content.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PostgreSQL and MySQL for a small SaaS application. Use the standard evaluation dimensions and state your recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear comparison with minimal context.

prompt_templates.title: Constraint-Based Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate Kafka, RabbitMQ, and Pulsar for high throughput, seven-day retention, Java expertise, and at-least-once delivery.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team has measurable technical and staffing constraints.

prompt_templates.title: POC Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a POC for Redis Streams versus Kafka. Define workload, metrics, failure tests, acceptance thresholds, risks, and the decision method.
prompt_templates.scenario: A platform team needs evidence before selecting a message system.

prompt_templates.title: Weighted Decision and ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weighted evaluation and ADR for Kubernetes ingress options. Include constraints, evidence gaps, sensitivity analysis, migration risks, and staged adoption.
prompt_templates.scenario: Architecture reviewers need an auditable decision for a shared platform.

output_examples.input: Compare Kafka and RabbitMQ for durable order events and traffic buffering.
output: Recommendation: Kafka for the core event stream.
Reason: It best matches sustained throughput, retention, and replay requirements.
Primary risk: Operational complexity requires monitoring and broker recovery tests.
Next step: Validate latency, recovery time, and consumer rebalancing in a POC.

output_examples.input: Evaluate two databases for a small team that needs simple operations and reliable transactions.
output: The report ranks transaction support, operational effort, ecosystem fit, cost, and team familiarity.
The recommendation names the preferred database and explains each important trade-off.
The risk section identifies migration, scaling, and skills gaps with practical mitigations.

best_practices: State workload, scale, compliance, budget, and team constraints before scoring candidates.
Replace generic weights with stakeholder-approved priorities and record the rationale.
Validate uncertain claims through a targeted POC with measurable acceptance thresholds.
anti_patterns: Do not select a technology using popularity or benchmark headlines alone.
Do not assign scores without evidence, assumptions, and explicit weighting.
Do not present a recommendation without risks, mitigations, and follow-up validation.

faq.question: What technologies can this skill compare?
faq.answer: It can compare frameworks, databases, middleware, messaging systems, infrastructure platforms, and other technical alternatives.

faq.question: Does the skill choose weights automatically?
faq.answer: It provides default dimensions, but stakeholders should adjust weights to match business and technical priorities.

faq.question: Can it produce an ADR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can convert the selected option, context, trade-offs, risks, and consequences into an ADR-ready decision.

faq.question: Does it run benchmarks or POCs?
faq.answer: No. It designs validation steps and acceptance criteria, but execution requires the target environment and engineering tools.

faq.question: How current is the technology information?
faq.answer: The skill uses provided context and model knowledge. Verify changing prices, versions, vulnerabilities, and community metrics with current sources.

faq.question: What information improves the evaluation?
faq.answer: Provide workload, scale, reliability targets, consistency needs, security rules, budget, existing systems, team skills, and migration constraints.
